served: trial of glucose correction with insulin
results: 1. blood glucose: 30.63 mmol/L (551.3 mg/dL) with glycosuria and NO ketonuria
2. HbA1c: very high on admission; 5.73% at first follow-up once glucose was controlled
3. CT head (non-contrast): HYPERDENSE LEFT caudate and lentiform nucleus - contralateral to the movements
4. brain MRI with contrast: a coexisting LACUNAR INFARCT in addition to the striatal signal change
5. trial of glucose correction with insulin: glucose fell to 5.9 mmol/L (106.2 mg/dL) at follow-up with improvement in the movements
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Non-ketotic hyperglycemia-induced hemichorea (diabetic striatopathy) caused by new-onset type 2 diabetes mellitus presenting as hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state.

Alternatives:
1. Hemiballismus secondary to the coexisting lacunar infarct in the contralateral striatum.
2. Hyperthyroidism-associated chorea.
3. Wilson's disease (acute neuroinflammatory presentation).
